subject: API commit elevation + latency SLA migration — EdgeCart renewal
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@edgecart.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-06-04T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal discussion — bumping monthly commit + rate limits

Karthik,

Appreciate the renewal reminder — we ran the May spike analysis and it looks like our hosted usage will grow ~2.6x over the next 12 months if conversion tests succeed. Two asks from our side as we prep the procurement bundle: 

- Can Redwood support a 3x monthly committed token uplift (current commit 2M tokens -> proposed 6M tokens) with a predictable softburst policy?
- We need a lane that reduces per-token rate at >4M monthly usage and an explicit latency SLO for conversational endpoints during peak traffic windows (p95 < 180ms).

Procurement is copied (procurement@edgecart.com) and wants an estimate for cost delta (monthly) and any SLA language we need to include. Also, can you attach recent usage CSVs for May?

Thanks — we’d like to lock terms this month if possible.

— Alex
Head of Product
EdgeCart, Inc.

Attachments referenced: EdgeCart_May_spikes.png (dashboard snapshot)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@edgecart.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-06-04T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — bumping monthly commit + rate limits

Alex — great to see the growth signal, congrats on the traction. High-level answers/upfront:

- We can support the 3x monthly committed token uplift (2M -> 6M) as a staged stepup with a 30-day telemetry validation window. We typically do a two-stage uplift to ensure cache warmup and batching profiles stabilize.
- We can add a tiered per-token rate that drops at your 4M and 5.5M thresholds. I’ll include exact pricing bands in the formal proposal.
- Latency SLO (p95 < 180ms) for your conversational route is achievable from hosted regions in us-west subject to a short warm-up period; we’ll include a seasonal SLA addendum for traffic spikes and an ops playbook for failover to a slightly lower-cost variant if capacity is constrained.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll send a draft proposal with pricing bands + DocuSign terms for the commit lift and the SLA addendum.
2) Loop in Grace and Marissa to confirm capacity allocation, provisioning lead times, and any temporary burst credits.
3) If procurement approves, we aim for a 2029-07-01 effective date with a 60-day migration window for routing and latency tuning.

I’ve attached an export of your May usage as requested and a one-page summary (see attachments).

Would you like us to include a softburst cushion for the first 90 days to absorb unanticipated spikes?

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0112

Attachments: EdgeCart-Usage-Report-May-2029.csv, RC-EdgeCart-Proposal-2029-06.pdf

From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-06-05T09:27:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal discussion — capacity planning notes

Karthik/Marissa/Vanessa — quick ops notes for the proposal: 

- Capacity: EdgeCart’s proposed committed uplift to 6M tokens/month maps to sustained throughput of ~210 tokens/s for their primary conversational route (accounting for bursty peak factor). Recommend reserving 2x baseline for headroom over 30 days during the staged uplift.
- Latency: To meet p95 < 180ms we need: GPU pool reservation in us-west-2 with the L2 kernel profile (I’ll flag RC-3821 for scheduling), and KV caching enabled across the route. Expect a 7–10 day tuning window after provisioning.
- Softburst: Ops can grant a 15% softburst cushion for the first 60 days; any overage beyond that will fall into burst billing per the proposal.

Questions: 
- Marissa: can finance confirm if we want the customer to prepay month 1 for the uplift or allow standard invoicing?
- Vanessa: any precedent on adding an SLA clause that includes a short-term credit ladder for missed latency targets during the initial 30-day warmup?

I’ll prepare a short ops checklist to include in the proposal.

— Grace
Sr. Technical Ops Manager
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@edgecart.com>, procurement@edgecart.com
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-06-06T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Final proposal and next steps — EdgeCart commit elevation (2M -> 6M)

Alex / Procurement — thanks for the quick sync. Attaching the formal proposal (RC-EdgeCart-Proposal-2029-06.pdf) and the May usage export. Summary of what’s in the doc: 

- Commit change: monthly committed tokens 2,000,000 -> 6,000,000; pricing bands included for 0-4M, 4M-5.5M, and >5.5M usage.
- Softburst policy: 15% cushion for first 60 days (no excess billing up to cushion); one-time grace window during the 30-day telemetry validation after uplift.
- Latency SLA: p95 < 180ms for /v1/chat/completions in us-west-2; initial 30-day warm-up where credits apply only if p95 misses the SLO by >25ms on average (language and examples included).
- Provisioning: ops will reserve the L2 kernel pool in us-west-2; expected 7–10 day provisioning + 10 days of tuning.
- Billing: proposed effective date 2029-07-01. Invoice terms: Net 30. We are open to requiring month-1 prepayment if Procurement prefers earlier commitment (Grace / Marissa, please advise).

Actions for Procurement / Alex: 
- Confirm acceptance of pricing bands and softburst cushion by EOD 2029-06-10.
- Sign the DocuSign envelope here: https://www.docusign.com/link/EdgeCart-Commit-2029

I will route the signed agreement to Finance and Ops for provisioning. If procurement needs alternate invoicing cadence or PO treatment, loop Marissa for billing exceptions.

Thanks — excited to scale with you.

Karthik Iyer
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Attachments: RC-EdgeCart-Proposal-2029-06.pdf, EdgeCart-Usage-Report-May-2029.csv
